q-159900.name: Question 1
q-159900.problem:
Let ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{18}$ be I.I.D. random variables with probability density function

$$
f(x;\theta )=\theta {x}^{-\theta -1},\,x\ge 1,
$$

where $\theta $ is an unknown parameter. For a particular sample ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{18},$ you're given that 

$$
{\prod }_{i=1}^{18}{x}_{i}=34.2.
$$

Find the likelihood function of the sample.
q-159900.worked_solution:
Recall that if ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ are independent and identically distributed continuous random variables with probability density function $f(x;\theta ),$ where $\theta $ is an unknown parameter, then the likelihood function of a random sample ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ is

$$
L(\theta )=P({X}_{1}={x}_{1},{X}_{2}={x}_{2},…,{X}_{n}={x}_{n})={\prod }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i};\,\theta ).
$$

In our case, we are given a sample of $n=18$ independent random variables with unknown parameter $\theta ,$ for which the probability density function is

$$
f(x;\theta )=\theta {x}^{-\theta -1},\,x\ge 1.
$$

We can calculate the likelihood function as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}L(\theta ) & ={\prod }_{i=1}^{n}(\theta {x}_{i}^{-\theta -1}) \\  & ={\theta }^{n}\cdot {\prod }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{-\theta -1} \\  & ={\theta }^{n}({\prod }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i})^{-\theta -1}\end{aligned}
$$

We are told that ${\prod }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}=34.2$ and $n=18.$ Therefore, 

$$
L(\theta )={\theta }^{18}(34.2)^{-\theta -1}.
$$

Let X1,X2,…,X12 be I.I.D. random variables with probability density function f(x;θ)=(θ+2)x−θ−3,x≥1, where θ is an unknown parameter. For a particular sample x1,x2,…,x12, you're given that ∏i=112xi=12.1. Find the likelihood function of the sample.

a
(θ+1)12(12.1)−θ−4
b
(θ+2)12.1(12)−θ−3
c
(θ+2)12.1(12)−θ−2
d
(θ+2)12(12.1)−θ−3
e
(θ+4)12(12.1)−θ−2
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Recall that if X1,X2,…,Xn are independent and identically distributed continuous random variables with probability density function f(x;θ), where θ is an unknown parameter, then the likelihood function of a random sample x1,x2,…,xn is

L(θ)=P(X1=x1,X2=x2,…,Xn=xn)=∏i=1nf(xi;θ).

In our case, we are given a sample of n=12 independent random variables with unknown parameter θ, for which the probability density function is

f(x;θ)=(θ+2)x−θ−3,x≥1.

We can calculate the likelihood function as follows:

L(θ)=∏i=1n((θ+2)xi−θ−3)=(θ+2)n⋅∏i=1nxi−θ−3=(θ+2)n(∏i=1nxi)−θ−3

We are told that ∏i=1nxi=12.1 and n=12. Therefore,

L(θ)=(θ+2)12(12.1)−θ−3.

q-159923.name: Question 3
q-159923.problem:
Let ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},{X}_{3}$ be I.I.D. random variables with probability density function

$$
f(x;\theta )=(\theta +2){x}^{-\theta -3},\,x\ge 1,
$$

where $\theta $ is an unknown parameter. Find the likelihood function of the sample $1.4,\,2.2,\,2.5.$
q-159923.worked_solution:
Recall that if ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ are independent and identically distributed continuous random variables with probability density function $f(x;\theta ),$ where $\theta $ is an unknown parameter, then the likelihood function of a random sample ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ is

$$
L(\theta )=P({X}_{1}={x}_{1},{X}_{2}={x}_{2},…,{X}_{n}={x}_{n})={\prod }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i};\,\theta ).
$$

In our case, we are given a sample of $n=3$ independent random variables with unknown parameter $\theta ,$ for which the probability density function is

$$
f(x;\theta )=(\theta +2){x}^{-\theta -3},\,x\ge 1.
$$

We can calculate the likelihood function as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}L(\theta ) & ={\prod }_{i=1}^{n}((\theta +2){x}_{i}^{-\theta -3}) \\  & =(\theta +2)^{n}\cdot {\prod }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{-\theta -3} \\  & =(\theta +2)^{n}({\prod }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i})^{-\theta -3}\end{aligned}
$$

For our sample, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\prod }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} & =1.4\cdot 2.2\cdot 2.5=7.7\end{aligned}
$$

and $n=3.$ Therefore, 

$$
L(\theta )=(\theta +2)^{3}(7.7)^{-\theta -3}.
$$

Question 3
?

Let X1,X2,X3 be I.I.D. random variables with probability density function f(x;θ)=(θ+2)x−θ−3,x≥1, where θ is an unknown parameter. Find the likelihood function of the sample 1.4,2.2,2.5.

a
(θ+2)4(6.1)−θ−3
b
(θ+2)3(7.7)−θ−3
c
(θ+2)3(6.1)−θ−3
d
(θ+2)7.7(3)−θ−3
e
(θ+2)3(6.1)−θ+3
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Recall that if X1,X2,…,Xn are independent and identically distributed continuous random variables with probability density function f(x;θ), where θ is an unknown parameter, then the likelihood function of a random sample x1,x2,…,xn is

L(θ)=P(X1=x1,X2=x2,…,Xn=xn)=∏i=1nf(xi;θ).

In our case, we are given a sample of n=3 independent random variables with unknown parameter θ, for which the probability density function is

f(x;θ)=(θ+2)x−θ−3,x≥1.

We can calculate the likelihood function as follows:

L(θ)=∏i=1n((θ+2)xi−θ−3)=(θ+2)n⋅∏i=1nxi−θ−3=(θ+2)n(∏i=1nxi)−θ−3

For our sample, we have that

∏i=1nxi=1.4⋅2.2⋅2.5=7.7

and n=3. Therefore,

L(θ)=(θ+2)3(7.7)−θ−3.

q-159849.name: Question 4
q-159849.problem:
Let ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},{X}_{3}$ be I.I.D. random variables with probability density function

$$
f(x;\theta )=\theta {x}^{-\theta -1},\,x\ge 1,
$$

where $\theta $ is an unknown parameter. Find the likelihood function of the sample $2.1,\,3.2,\,5.0.$
q-159849.worked_solution:
Recall that if ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ are independent and identically distributed continuous random variables with probability density function $f(x;\theta ),$ where $\theta $ is an unknown parameter, then the likelihood function of a random sample ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ is

$$
L(\theta )=P({X}_{1}={x}_{1},{X}_{2}={x}_{2},…,{X}_{n}={x}_{n})={\prod }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i};\,\theta ).
$$

In our case, we are given a sample of $n=3$ independent random variables with unknown parameter $\theta ,$ for which the probability density function is

$$
f(x;\theta )=\theta {x}^{-\theta -1},\,x\ge 1.
$$

We can calculate the likelihood function as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}L(\theta ) & ={\prod }_{i=1}^{n}(\theta {x}_{i}^{-\theta -1}) \\  & ={\theta }^{n}\cdot {\prod }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{-\theta -1} \\  & ={\theta }^{n}({\prod }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i})^{-\theta -1}\end{aligned}
$$

For our sample, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\prod }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} & =2.1\cdot 3.2\cdot 5.0=33.6\end{aligned}
$$

and $n=3.$ Therefore, 

$$
L(\theta )={\theta }^{3}(33.6)^{-\theta -1}.
$$

q-159921.name: Question 5
q-159921.problem:
Let ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},{X}_{3}$ be I.I.D. random variables with probability density function

$$
f(x;\theta )=(\theta +1){x}^{-\theta -2},\,x\ge 1,
$$

where $\theta $ is an unknown parameter. Find the likelihood function of the sample $1.2,\,1.5,\,2.5.$
q-159921.worked_solution:
Recall that if ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ are independent and identically distributed continuous random variables with probability density function $f(x;\theta ),$ where $\theta $ is an unknown parameter, then the likelihood function of a random sample ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ is

$$
L(\theta )=P({X}_{1}={x}_{1},{X}_{2}={x}_{2},…,{X}_{n}={x}_{n})={\prod }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i};\,\theta ).
$$

In our case, we are given a sample of $n=3$ independent random variables with unknown parameter $\theta ,$ for which the probability density function is

$$
f(x;\theta )=(\theta +1){x}^{-\theta -2},\,x\ge 1.
$$

We can calculate the likelihood function as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}L(\theta ) & ={\prod }_{i=1}^{n}((\theta +1){x}_{i}^{-\theta -2}) \\  & =(\theta +1)^{n}\cdot {\prod }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{-\theta -2} \\  & =(\theta +1)^{n}({\prod }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i})^{-\theta -2}\end{aligned}
$$

For our sample, we have that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\prod }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} & =1.2\cdot 1.5\cdot 2.5=4.5\end{aligned}
$$

and $n=3.$ Therefore, 

$$

Question 5
?

Let X1,X2,X3 be I.I.D. random variables with probability density function f(x;θ)=(θ+1)x−θ−2,x≥1, where θ is an unknown parameter. Find the likelihood function of the sample 1.2,1.5,2.5.

a
(θ+1)4(3)−θ−2
b
(θ+1)(4.5)−θ−2
c
(θ+1)4.5(4)−θ−2
d
(θ+1)3(4.5)−θ−2
e
(θ+1)(4)−θ−2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Recall that if X1,X2,…,Xn are independent and identically distributed continuous random variables with probability density function f(x;θ), where θ is an unknown parameter, then the likelihood function of a random sample x1,x2,…,xn is

L(θ)=P(X1=x1,X2=x2,…,Xn=xn)=∏i=1nf(xi;θ).

In our case, we are given a sample of n=3 independent random variables with unknown parameter θ, for which the probability density function is

f(x;θ)=(θ+1)x−θ−2,x≥1.

We can calculate the likelihood function as follows:

L(θ)=∏i=1n((θ+1)xi−θ−2)=(θ+1)n⋅∏i=1nxi−θ−2=(θ+1)n(∏i=1nxi)−θ−2

For our sample, we have that

∏i=1nxi=1.2⋅1.5⋅2.5=4.5

and n=3. Therefore,

L(θ)=(θ+1)3(4.5)−θ−2.

q-159873.problem:
Suppose ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{9}$ is an I.I.D random sample with ${X}_{i}∼\text{Exp}(\theta )$ and unknown rate parameter $\theta .$ For a particular sample ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{9},$ you're given that 

$$
{\sum }_{i=1}^{9}{x}_{i}=15.
$$

Find the likelihood function of the sample.

*Hint: The probability density function for an exponential random variable is given by* 

$$
f(x;\theta )=\theta {e}^{-\theta x},\,x\ge 0.
$$
q-159873.worked_solution:
Recall that if ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ are independent and identically distributed continuous random variables with probability density function $f(x;\theta ),$ where $\theta $ is an unknown parameter, then the likelihood function of a random sample ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ is

$$
L(\theta )=P({X}_{1}={x}_{1},{X}_{2}={x}_{2},…,{X}_{n}={x}_{n})={\prod }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i};\,\theta ).
$$

In our case, we are given a sample of $n=9$ independent exponential random variables with unknown parameter $\theta ,$ for which the probability density function is

$$
f(x;\theta )=\theta {e}^{-\theta x},\,x\ge 0.
$$

We can calculate the likelihood function as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}L(\theta ) & ={\prod }_{i=1}^{n}\theta {e}^{-\theta {x}_{i}} \\  & ={\theta }^{n}\,{e}^{-\theta \sum {x}_{i}} \\  & ={\theta }^{n}\,{e}^{-S\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

where $S={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}.$ 

We are told that $S={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}=15$ and $n=9.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}L(\theta ) & ={\theta }^{9}\,{e}^{-15\theta }.\end{aligned}
$$

q-159881.name: Question 10
q-159881.problem: Suppose ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},{X}_{3}$ is an I.I.D random sample with ${X}_{i}∼\text{Exp}(\theta )$ and unknown rate parameter $\theta .$ Find the likelihood function of the sample $1.3,\,4.3,\,2.4.$
q-159881.worked_solution:
Recall that if ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ are independent and identically distributed continuous random variables with probability density function $f(x;\theta ),$ where $\theta $ is an unknown parameter, then the likelihood function of a random sample ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ is

$$
L(\theta )=P({X}_{1}={x}_{1},{X}_{2}={x}_{2},…,{X}_{n}={x}_{n})={\prod }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i};\,\theta ).
$$

In our case, we are given a sample of $n=3$ independent exponential random variables with unknown parameter $\theta ,$ for which the probability density function is

$$
f(x;\theta )=\theta {e}^{-\theta x},\,x\ge 0.
$$

We can calculate the likelihood function as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}L(\theta ) & ={\prod }_{i=1}^{n}\theta {e}^{-\theta {x}_{i}} \\  & ={\theta }^{n}\,{e}^{-\theta \sum {x}_{i}} \\  & ={\theta }^{n}\,{e}^{-S\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

where $S={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}.$ 

For our sample, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}S & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =1.3+4.3+2.4 \\  & =8.0\end{aligned}
$$

and $n=3.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}L(\theta ) & ={\theta }^{3}\,{e}^{-8\theta }.\end{aligned}
$$

q-159953.name: Question 11
q-159953.problem:
Suppose ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{10}$ is an I.I.D random sample with ${X}_{i}∼N(\theta ,1),$ where $\theta $ is an unknown mean. For a particular sample ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{10},$ you're given that 

$$
{\sum }_{i=1}^{10}{x}_{i}=-2.8,\,{\sum }_{i=1}^{10}{x}_{i}^{2}=14.24.
$$

Given that the likelihood function of the sample is

$$
L(\theta )=\frac{1}{32{\pi }^{5}}\,{e}^{\,g(\theta )},
$$

what is the expression for $g(\theta )?$

*Hint: The probability density function for a normal random variable with mean $\theta $ and variance $1$ is given by* 

$$
f(x;\theta )=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi }}{e}^{-(x-\theta )^{2}/2},\,x\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$
q-159953.worked_solution:
Recall that if ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ are independent and identically distributed continuous random variables with probability density function $f(x;\theta ),$ where $\theta $ is an unknown parameter, then the likelihood function of a random sample ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ is

$$
L(\theta )=P({X}_{1}={x}_{1},{X}_{2}={x}_{2},…,{X}_{n}={x}_{n})={\prod }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i};\,\theta ).
$$

In our case, we are given a sample of $n=10$ independent normal random variables with unknown mean $\theta $ and variance ${\sigma }^{2}=1,$ for which the probability density function is

$$
f(x;\theta )=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi }}{e}^{-(x-\theta )^{2}/2},\,x\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

We can calculate the likelihood function as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}L(\theta ) & ={\prod }_{i=1}^{n}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi }}{e}^{-({x}_{i}-\theta )^{2}/2}) \\  & =(2\pi )^{-n/2}\,{e}^{-\sum ({x}_{i}-\theta )^{2}/2} \\  & =(2\pi )^{-n/2}\,{e}^{-(\sum {x}_{i}^{2}-2\theta \sum {x}_{i}+n{\theta }^{2})/2} \\  & =(2\pi )^{-n/2}\,{e}^{-(C-2S\theta +n{\theta }^{2})/2}\end{aligned}
$$

where $S={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}$ and $C={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2}.$

We are told that $S={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}=-2.8,$ $C={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2}=14.24,$ and $n=10.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}L(\theta ) & =(2\pi )^{-10/2}\,{e}^{-(14.24-2(-2.8)\theta +10{\theta }^{2})/2} \\  & =\frac{1}{32{\pi }^{5}}\,{e}^{\,-7.12\,-\,2.8\theta \,-\,5{\theta }^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$

L(θ)=P(X1=x1,X2=x2,…,Xn=xn)=∏i=1nf(xi;θ).

f(x;θ)=12πe−(x−θ)2/2,x∈(−∞,∞).

We can calculate the likelihood function as follows:

L(θ)=∏i=1n(12πe−(xi−θ)2/2)=(2π)−n/2e−∑(xi−θ)2/2=(2π)−n/2e−(∑xi2−2θ∑xi+nθ2)/2=(2π)−n/2e−(C−2Sθ+nθ2)/2

where S=∑i=1nxi and C=∑i=1nxi2.

We are told that S=∑i=1nxi=−2.8, C=∑i=1nxi2=14.24, and n=10. Therefore,

L(θ)=(2π)−10/2e−(14.24−2(−2.8)θ+10θ2)/2=132π5e−7.12−2.8θ−5θ2.

Therefore,

g(θ)=−7.12−2.8θ−5θ2.

q-159950.problem:
Suppose ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{8}$ is an I.I.D random sample with ${X}_{i}∼N(\theta ,1),$  where $\theta $ is an unknown mean. For a particular sample ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{8},$ you're given that 

$$
{\sum }_{i=1}^{8}{x}_{i}=5.6,\,{\sum }_{i=1}^{8}{x}_{i}^{2}=7.8.
$$

Given that the likelihood function of the sample is

$$
L(\theta )=\frac{1}{16{\pi }^{4}}\,{e}^{\,g(\theta )},
$$

what is the expression for $g(\theta )?$

*Hint: The probability density function for a normal random variable with mean $\theta $ and variance $1$ is given by* 

$$
f(x;\theta )=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi }}{e}^{-(x-\theta )^{2}/2},\,x\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$
q-159950.worked_solution:
Recall that if ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ are independent and identically distributed continuous random variables with probability density function $f(x;\theta ),$ where $\theta $ is an unknown parameter, then the likelihood function of a random sample ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ is

$$
L(\theta )=P({X}_{1}={x}_{1},{X}_{2}={x}_{2},…,{X}_{n}={x}_{n})={\prod }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i};\,\theta ).
$$

In our case, we are given a sample of $n=8$ independent normal random variables with unknown mean $\theta $ and variance ${\sigma }^{2}=1,$ for which the probability density function is

$$
f(x;\theta )=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi }}{e}^{-(x-\theta )^{2}/2},\,x\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

We can calculate the likelihood function as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}L(\theta ) & ={\prod }_{i=1}^{n}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi }}{e}^{-({x}_{i}-\theta )^{2}/2}) \\  & =(2\pi )^{-n/2}\,{e}^{-\sum ({x}_{i}-\theta )^{2}/2} \\  & =(2\pi )^{-n/2}\,{e}^{-(\sum {x}_{i}^{2}-2\theta \sum {x}_{i}+n{\theta }^{2})/2} \\  & =(2\pi )^{-n/2}\,{e}^{-(C-2S\theta +n{\theta }^{2})/2}\end{aligned}
$$

where $S={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}$ and $C={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2}.$

We are told that $S={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}=5.6,$ $C={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2}=7.8,$ and $n=8.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}L(\theta ) & =(2\pi )^{-8/2}\,{e}^{-(7.8-2(5.6)\theta +8{\theta }^{2})/2} \\  & =\frac{1}{16{\pi }^{4}}\,{e}^{\,-3.9\,+\,5.6\theta \,-\,4{\theta }^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
g(\theta )=-3.9+5.6\theta -4{\theta }^{2}.
$$

$$
L(\theta )=P({X}_{1}={x}_{1},{X}_{2}={x}_{2},…,{X}_{n}={x}_{n})={\prod }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i};\,\theta ).
$$

In our case, we are given a sample of $n=6$ independent normal random variables with unknown mean $\theta $ and variance ${\sigma }^{2}=1,$ for which the probability density function is

$$
f(x;\theta )=\frac{1}{\sigma \sqrt{2\pi }}{e}^{-\frac{1}{2}{(\frac{x-\theta }{\sigma })}^{2}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi }}{e}^{-(x-\theta )^{2}/2},\,x\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}L(\theta ) & ={\prod }_{i=1}^{n}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi }}{e}^{-({x}_{i}-\theta )^{2}/2}) \\  & =(2\pi )^{-n/2}\,{e}^{-\sum ({x}_{i}-\theta )^{2}/2} \\  & =(2\pi )^{-n/2}\,{e}^{-(\sum {x}_{i}^{2}-2\theta \sum {x}_{i}+n{\theta }^{2})/2} \\  & =(2\pi )^{-n/2}\,{e}^{-(C-2S\theta +n{\theta }^{2})/2}\end{aligned}
$$

where $S={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}$ and $C={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}S & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =4.8+0.7+5+2.7+1.9+2.7 \\  & =17.8 \\ C & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2} \\  & =(4.8)^{2}+(0.7)^{2}+(5)^{2}+(2.7)^{2}+(1.9)^{2}+(2.7)^{2} \\  & =66.72\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}L(\theta ) & =(2\pi )^{-6/2}\,{e}^{-(66.72-2(17.8)\theta +6{\theta }^{2})/2} \\  & =\frac{1}{8{\pi }^{3}}\,{e}^{\,-33.36\,+\,17.8\theta \,-\,3{\theta }^{2}}.\end{aligned}

$$

$$
L(\theta )=P({X}_{1}={x}_{1},{X}_{2}={x}_{2},…,{X}_{n}={x}_{n})={\prod }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i};\,\theta ).
$$

$$
f(x;\theta )=\frac{1}{\sigma \sqrt{2\pi }}{e}^{-\frac{1}{2}{(\frac{x-\theta }{\sigma })}^{2}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi }}{e}^{-(x-\theta )^{2}/2},\,x\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}L(\theta ) & ={\prod }_{i=1}^{n}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi }}{e}^{-({x}_{i}-\theta )^{2}/2}) \\  & =(2\pi )^{-n/2}\,{e}^{-\sum ({x}_{i}-\theta )^{2}/2} \\  & =(2\pi )^{-n/2}\,{e}^{-(\sum {x}_{i}^{2}-2\theta \sum {x}_{i}+n{\theta }^{2})/2} \\  & =(2\pi )^{-n/2}\,{e}^{-(C-2S\theta +n{\theta }^{2})/2}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}S & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =0.8+(-0.8)+0.6+0.9+2.4 \\  & =3.9 \\ C & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2} \\  & =(0.8)^{2}+(-0.8)^{2}+(0.6)^{2}+(0.9)^{2}+(2.4)^{2} \\  & =8.21\end{aligned}

Suppose X1,X2,X3,X4,X5 is an I.I.D random sample with Xi∼N(θ,1), where θ is an unknown mean. Given that the likelihood function of the sample 0.8,−0.8,0.6,0.9,2.4 is L(θ)=1(2π)5/2eg(θ), what is the expression for g(θ)?

a
−4.105+3.9θ−2.5θ2
b
−7.57+3.9θ−5θ2
c
−2.45+3.9θ−2.5θ2
d
−7.57+3.9θ−2.5θ2
e
−3.78+3.9θ−2.5θ2
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Recall that if X1,X2,…,Xn are independent and identically distributed continuous random variables with probability density function f(x;θ), where θ is an unknown parameter, then the likelihood function of a random sample x1,x2,…,xn is

L(θ)=P(X1=x1,X2=x2,…,Xn=xn)=∏i=1nf(xi;θ).

In our case, we are given a sample of n=5 independent normal random variables with unknown mean θ and variance σ2=1, for which the probability density function is

f(x;θ)=1σ2πe−12(x−θσ)2=12πe−(x−θ)2/2,x∈(−∞,∞).

We can calculate the likelihood function as follows:

L(θ)=∏i=1n(12πe−(xi−θ)2/2)=(2π)−n/2e−∑(xi−θ)2/2=(2π)−n/2e−(∑xi2−2θ∑xi+nθ2)/2=(2π)−n/2e−(C−2Sθ+nθ2)/2

where S=∑i=1nxi and C=∑i=1nxi2.

For our sample, we have that

S=∑i=1nxi=0.8+(−0.8)+0.6+0.9+2.4=3.9C=∑i=1nxi2=(0.8)2+(−0.8)2+(0.6)2+(0.9)2+(2.4)2=8.21

and n=5. Therefore,

L(θ)=(2π)−5/2e−(8.21−2(3.9)θ+5θ2)/2=1(2π)5/2e−4.105+3.9θ−2.5θ2.

Therefore,

g(θ)=−4.105+3.9θ−2.5θ2.

q-159955.problem:
Suppose ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},{X}_{3},{X}_{4},{X}_{5}$ is an I.I.D random sample with ${X}_{i}∼N(\theta ,1),$  where $\theta $ is an unknown mean.  Given that the likelihood function of the sample $1.3,\,0.2,\,2.3,\,-0.7,\,0.9$ is

$$
L(\theta )=\frac{1}{(2\pi )^{5/2}}\,{e}^{\,g(\theta )},
$$

what is the expression for $g(\theta )?$
q-159955.worked_solution:
Recall that if ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ are independent and identically distributed continuous random variables with probability density function $f(x;\theta ),$ where $\theta $ is an unknown parameter, then the likelihood function of a random sample ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ is

$$
L(\theta )=P({X}_{1}={x}_{1},{X}_{2}={x}_{2},…,{X}_{n}={x}_{n})={\prod }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i};\,\theta ).
$$

In our case, we are given a sample of $n=5$ independent normal random variables with unknown mean $\theta $ and variance ${\sigma }^{2}=1,$ for which the probability density function is

$$
f(x;\theta )=\frac{1}{\sigma \sqrt{2\pi }}{e}^{-\frac{1}{2}{(\frac{x-\theta }{\sigma })}^{2}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi }}{e}^{-(x-\theta )^{2}/2},\,x\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

We can calculate the likelihood function as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}L(\theta ) & ={\prod }_{i=1}^{n}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi }}{e}^{-({x}_{i}-\theta )^{2}/2}) \\  & =(2\pi )^{-n/2}\,{e}^{-\sum ({x}_{i}-\theta )^{2}/2} \\  & =(2\pi )^{-n/2}\,{e}^{-(\sum {x}_{i}^{2}-2\theta \sum {x}_{i}+n{\theta }^{2})/2} \\  & =(2\pi )^{-n/2}\,{e}^{-(C-2S\theta +n{\theta }^{2})/2}\end{aligned}
$$

where $S={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}$ and $C={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2}.$

For our sample, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}S & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =1.3+0.2+2.7+(-0.7)+0.9 \\  & =4 \\ C & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2} \\  & =(1.3)^{2}+(0.2)^{2}+(2.3)^{2}+(-0.7)^{2}+(0.9)^{2} \\  & =8.32\end{aligned}
$$

and $n=5.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}L(\theta ) & =(2\pi )^{-5/2}\,{e}^{-(8.32-2(4)\theta +5{\theta }^{2})/2} \\  & =\frac{1}{(2\pi )^{5/2}}\,{e}^{\,-4.16\,+\,4\theta \,-\,2.5{\theta }^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
g(\theta )=-4.16+4\theta -2.5{\theta }^{2}.
$$

Recall that if X1,X2,…,Xn are independent and identically distributed continuous random variables with probability density function f(x;θ), where θ is an unknown parameter, then the likelihood function of a random sample x1,x2,…,xn is

L(θ)=P(X1=x1,X2=x2,…,Xn=xn)=∏i=1nf(xi;θ).

In our case, we are given a sample of n=5 independent normal random variables with unknown mean θ and variance σ2=1, for which the probability density function is

f(x;θ)=1σ2πe−12(x−θσ)2=12πe−(x−θ)2/2,x∈(−∞,∞).

We can calculate the likelihood function as follows:

L(θ)=∏i=1n(12πe−(xi−θ)2/2)=(2π)−n/2e−∑(xi−θ)2/2=(2π)−n/2e−(∑xi2−2θ∑xi+nθ2)/2=(2π)−n/2e−(C−2Sθ+nθ2)/2

where S=∑i=1nxi and C=∑i=1nxi2.

For our sample, we have that

S=∑i=1nxi=1.3+0.2+2.7+(−0.7)+0.9=4C=∑i=1nxi2=(1.3)2+(0.2)2+(2.3)2+(−0.7)2+(0.9)2=8.32

and n=5. Therefore,

L(θ)=(2π)−5/2e−(8.32−2(4)θ+5θ2)/2=1(2π)5/2e−4.16+4θ−2.5θ2.

Therefore,

g(θ)=−4.16+4θ−2.5θ2.
